messages:
elena: quick sanity check — onboarding the v2-rerank (int8) runs looks fine latency-wise but ndcg dropped ~3-4% on devset A. anyone seen a provenance/sampling tilt lately?

samir: can you paste the eval command and which split? devset A is the cheap web scrape one (75k queries) — last run used deduped docs?

elena: ran: `python eval/rerank_eval.py --model v2-rerank-int8 --split devA --topk 100 --metrics ndcg,mrr`
elena: provenance: candidate pool was from gen-2025-02 (approx). no dedupe step this time, we kept original candidate ids.

jo: small note — dedup/no-dedup can shift ndcg when duplicates inflate clicky docs. that could explain a 3-4% change. did you also change doc truncation?

elena: ah — i toggled prep to keep full doc bodies (previously truncated at 512 tokens). trying an ablation now with truncation back to 512 and with dedupe.

li: another angle — formatting differences matter: we had a preproc change that replaced newlines with spaces and stripped bullets. the reranker learned to use layout signals.

elena: good call. here's a quick diff of query/doc forms that might be impacting:```
query: "how to install redis"
doc_a: "Redis — Installation on macOS

Steps:
1. brew install redis
2. ..."
doc_b: "Redis — Installation on macOS. Steps: 1. brew install redis 2. ..."
```

ryan: formatting collapse can reduce useful anchor tokens. also tokenization with the new tokenizer + quantized model might produce different token boundaries, which impacts softmax scores.

samir: is eval-bot showing any metric drift alerts for other slices? @eval-bot any recent runs flagged?

eval-bot: flagged_runs: ["1734890000", "1734923333"] | flag_reasons: ["ndcg_drop_devA", "tokenization_mismatch"]

jo: suggestion: run 3 quick ablations in parallel: (A) revert newline->space, (B) re-enable dedupe, (C) trunc=512 + re-tokenize. keep same candidate pool. compare ndcg@10 and mrr@10.

elena: on it. kicking off. will post a tiny table when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ryan: also capture candidate provenance per-query (ids) — we may see that certain queries lost high-quality docs because candidate generation switched to a cheaper sparse pass last week.

elena: noted. if ablation points at formatting, we'll add a preprocessing compat flag for model onboarding so new formats don't silently regress older evals.

samir: nice. if it's quantization-specific, we should compare float16 run on the same inputs too — to separate quantization vs formatting effects.

elena: plan: float16 baseline + int8 current + three ablations. will post results in this thread in ~45m.

li: +1. also include a tiny example where ndcg flips (one query) so we can inspect ranking lists. those examples are the fastest clue.

elena: will attach top-5 lists per run. thanks all.
